answer: Colorectal cancer screening should begin at age 45 for average-risk adults, according to the USPSTF. Screening is recommended until age 75. Options include colonoscopy every 10 years, annual FIT testing, or stool DNA-FIT every 1-3 years [USPSTF, 2021].

results.content: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in all adults aged 45 to 75 years. Screening options include colonoscopy every 10 years, annual FIT testing, or stool DNA-FIT every 1-3 years.

The USPSTF recommends cervical cancer screening every 3 years with cytology alone for women aged 21-29, and for women aged 30-65, every 5 years with high-risk HPV testing (alone or with cytology) or every 3 years with cytology alone.
